resources.string: Import any Android project as a ZIP file
Analyze and validate the project on your phone
Push it to your GitHub repository
Build it in the cloud and download the Debug APK
ApkStudio builds your project inside your own GitHub account, so you need to link it once using a personal access token.
How to create a token (one minute)
1. Tap the button below to open GitHub in your browser.
2. Give the token a name such as “ApkStudio” and choose an expiry date.
3. Enable the “repo” scope and the “workflow” scope, then generate the token.
4. Copy the token, come back here, paste it and tap “Link GitHub account”.
Required scopes: repo + workflow. The token is stored encrypted on your phone only and is never shared.
Create a new repository or check the account you linked.
Public repo: cloud builds are unlimited and free.
Private repo: builds use your free GitHub Actions minutes (2000 min/month).
Please enter a valid name (letters, numbers, - _ .).
Select the ZIP file of your Android project. ApkStudio will unpack and analyze it before uploading.
The ZIP must contain a complete Android (Gradle) project.
Unpacking the ZIP and inspecting the project structure.
No warnings — the project looks good.
Pushing project files and the cloud-build workflow to your repository.
You can leave this screen — the build continues on GitHub. Come back to download your APK.
The build is queued and usually starts within a minute.
A copy was also saved to your Downloads folder.
Allow ApkStudio to install apps, then come back and tap Install again.

ApkStudio turns an Android project ZIP into a Debug APK: it analyzes the project on your phone, pushes it to your GitHub repository, builds it with GitHub Actions, and downloads the result back to you.
Your GitHub token will be removed from this phone. You can link your account again at any time.
The phone could not reach api.github.com.
Check your Wi-Fi or mobile data, then retry.
Your connection is slow or GitHub is busy. Retry in a moment.
Check your date/time settings or try another network, then retry.
Your token is wrong, expired or revoked. Create a new token and link your account again.
Too many requests in a short time. Wait a few minutes and retry. Large projects consume more requests.
Your token needs the “repo” and “workflow” scopes. Create a new token with both scopes and link again.
Check that your account has access to this repository and that the token has the “repo” and “workflow” scopes.
The repository, branch, workflow or build run was not found. It may have been renamed or deleted.
The build could not start because Actions is turned off for this repository.
On GitHub, open the repository → Settings → Actions → General, and allow actions to run. Then rebuild.
Check the technical details below. The workflow file may be missing — try uploading the project again.
The repository state changed unexpectedly. Retry, and if it persists, use a new empty repository.
Retry. If the problem persists, check the technical details or try again later.
The selected file is corrupted or is not a valid ZIP archive.
Re-export the project as ZIP (without password) and try again.
No settings.gradle / build.gradle structure was found in the archive.
Make sure the ZIP contains the full Android Studio project folder (the one with settings.gradle and the app folder).
The project has no com.android.application module, so no APK can be produced.
Make sure the project contains an app module (e.g. the “app” folder with build.gradle).
The build finished but uploaded no artifacts.
This usually means the Gradle build step failed silently. Check the build log and rebuild.
This build result expired on GitHub. Rebuild the project to get a fresh APK.
Check your connection and storage space, then retry the download.
The downloaded archive did not contain any .apk file.
Rebuild the project. If it persists, check the build log for packaging errors.
Check your connection and token permissions (repo + workflow), then retry the upload.
Make sure GitHub Actions is enabled for the repository and the workflow file was uploaded, then retry.
ApkStudio triggered the workflow but no build run appeared on GitHub.
Open the repository on GitHub → Actions tab, and check that the “ApkStudio Build” workflow exists and Actions is enabled.
Retry. If it keeps happening, try a new empty repository.
Notifications when a cloud build finishes
Your Debug APK is ready to download.
Open ApkStudio to see the exact error.
No Gradle wrapper (gradlew) found — the cloud build will use a system Gradle fallback, which may fail on old projects.
gradlew exists but gradle-wrapper.jar is missing — the cloud build may fail. Export the full project folder.
Old Android Gradle Plugin (%1$s) — the cloud build uses a compatible JDK automatically, but old projects may still fail.
Old Gradle version (%1$s) detected — modern JDKs cannot run it, so JDK 11 will be used.
The project applies the Google Services plugin but has no google-services.json — the cloud build will fail unless you add it.
%1$d file(s) are larger than %2$s and will be skipped during upload.
Could not detect AGP/Gradle versions — modern defaults will be used and old projects may fail.
